title: Consolidated console interaction fact-graph + denormalized access patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: ad-hoc console queries and dashboards are slow and costly because event payloads are highly normalized and sessionization logic is duplicated across consumers. Current table design forces wide JOINs for route-level cost & latency attribution and blocks simple time-window rollups.

Proposal: introduce a small set of purpose-built 'interaction fact' denormalized tables backed by an event-to-fact transformation pipeline. The fact-graph model records interaction primitives (route_invocation, route_response, route_error, embed_call) with late-binding dimension keys and sparse dimensionization to keep row width low for most rows. We will maintain separate materialized dimension tables for tenant, route_config, model_variant and deployment_context that are joined at query time for heavy analytical queries but pre-joined for common dashboard paths.

Goals:
- Reduce median dashboard query latency by 3-5x for top 50 queries
- Lower per-query scan bytes for common slices (tenant/week/route) by 40%
- Centralize sessionization and attribution logic to avoid drift across consumers
- Provide clear data contracts and migration strategy for downstream BI and alerts
acceptance_criteria: New interaction_fact_v1 table exists in analytics dataset with schema documented in Confluence
Top 25 dashboard queries on Grafana migrated to use interaction_fact_v1 with >=2x latency improvement
Automated ETL/CDC job produces idempotent daily partitions with backfill completed for last 12 months
Data contract published with example queries, SLA for freshness, and migration checklist; stakeholders sign-off
Cost projection run comparing storage & query cost for 12 months showing net neutral or improved spend

progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with PM, Analytics, Data Eng and SRE. Agreed on late-binding dimensions and sparse columns for optional metadata.
2026-03-03: Prototype SQL for route_invocation factorization completed; improved a sample dashboard query latency from 14s to 3.2s in dev cluster.
2026-03-08: Discovered an edge case where streamed embed calls have variable tokenization; added normalization step to ETL plan.
2026-03-12: Confluence draft published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Interaction+Fact+Graph. Requested sign-off from analytics and console PMs.
2026-03-14: Began writing dbt model and unit tests; created GH draft PR for transformation logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/data-platform/pull/487
notes_for_review: Key trade-offs: pre-joining will speed common queries but increases storage and ETL cost. We choose late-binding for less-used dimensions (e.g., model tags) to avoid width explosion. Need analytics owners to validate parity before full switch-over. Also recommend a 6-week parallel run window for metric drift detection.
